title: Canonical Component Compass and Variant Token Catalog for Rollout Surfaces
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a canonical reference (Component Compass) and a Variant Token Catalog focused on rollout surfaces: dashboard cards, rollout rails, cost summary widgets, and multistate legends. Deliverables include a Figma kit, exportable token JSON, developer handoff notes, and a short prototype demonstrating state transitions and token swaps during canary/A-B rollouts.
background: Console rollout surfaces have accumulated ad-hoc variants and token overrides across several feature launches. This has led to inconsistent spacing, elevation, and status coloring in canary and rollout states, which confuses users and makes QA + front-end implementation brittle. We need a single source-of-truth artifact that designers and engineers can rely on when creating or reviewing rollout UX.
goals: Define a minimal set of tokens that cover rollout states (idle, pending, canary, rollout, degraded), density variants (compact, default, spacious), and cost-focused accent rules.
Provide component compass pages that map each console surface to recommended component variants and tokens.
Ship a Figma library with production-ready components and exportable tokens JSON for engineering consumption.
Reduce rollout visual regressions by providing a checklist and automated token linting suggestions for PRs.
success_metrics: Reduction in visual regressions reported in QA for rollout surfaces by 60% in 6 weeks
Decrease in frontend styling PR review cycles for rollout components by 30%
Adoption: 90% of new rollout-related tickets reference the Component Compass in design reviews within 2 cycles
deliverables: Figma library: 'Compass - Rollout Surfaces' with tokens and components
Exportable tokens JSON with namespaced keys (tokens.console.rollout.*)
Prototype demonstrating a canary -> rollout -> fallback transition with token swaps
Design handoff doc with implementation notes and accessibility checks
Checklist for Console UX reviewers and a short Loom demo
design_notes: Key decisions: use semantic token names scoped to surface and state (e.g., token.surface.card.bg.idle, token.surface.card.bg.canary); prefer a 3-step color ramp for status accents (neutral -> warning -> critical) instead of many single-purpose hues; adopt 8px baseline spacing with well-defined compact overrides; ensure elevation tokens map to Material-like z-values but expressed as semantic tokens for surface purpose.
figma_file: Figma: Redwood Console / Compass - Rollout Surfaces (Team Library)
accessibility_notes: All color token swaps must maintain a contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for text on background in default and compact density; status icons require text alternatives and ARIA-live regions for rollout state changes. Prototype includes screen-reader narration script to validate transitions.
implementation_notes: Provide a tokens.json that maps to CSS custom properties and Tailwind variables. Engineers should import tokens.console.rollout.* and avoid hardcoded hex values in components. Provide example component props for 'density' and 'rolloutState' with mapping table in handoff doc.
risks: If the tokens schema is not aligned with the engineering export pipeline, adoption will stall. There's also a risk that too many token variants will reintroduce fragmentation — keep the catalog intentionally small.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library published to team library and components are marked as production-ready
tokens.json exported and validated by ENG tokens-export-cli with sample mapping in the PR
Prototype demonstrates all five rollout states and density variants with accessible transitions
Handoff doc reviewed and signed off by Product, Engineering, and Accessibility leads
